sources: 2-(2-methoxyethoxy)ethanol is a chemical compound used as a fuel system icing inhibitor in jet fuels and as an industrial solvent in construction products (paints/stains, caulks/sealants), cosmetic products, high-strength cleansers, automotive fluids, and certain inks.

Acenaphthene is a C12 PAH produced during combustion and manufactured for industrial uses. Combustion sources include the burning of fossil fuels, forest fires, volcanic eruptions, and charbroiling of food. Industrially, it is an intermediate used in the production of dyes, plastics, biocides, and pharmaceutical products.

Acenaphthylene is a C12 PAH produced during combustion and also manufactured for industrial uses. Combustion sources include the burning of fossil fuels, forest fires, volcanic eruptions, and charbroiling of food. It is used in insecticides, fungicides, and as an intermediate in the manufacture of dyes and plastics.

Alachlor is a synthetic herbicide used in agriculture. It has been used extensively in pre-emergent weed control formulations in crops such as corn, sorghum, and soybeans. It enters drinking water primarily from agricultural runoff.

Anthracene is a diesel-range PAH (C14) found in coal tar and produced by incomplete combustion processes. It is used in production of dyes and as a component of synthetic fibers and plastics. It occurs in tobacco smoke, vehicle emissions, and other combustion gasses, and is found in surface waters, waste waters, and lake sediments.

Antimony is a chemical element found naturally in the form of the mineral stibnite (antimony trisulfide). Pure antimony is used in alloys for solders and a variety of metals, while antimony-containing compounds are commonly used in fire retardants, plastics, textiles, rubber, adhesives, ceramics, paint, and paper. Antimony is also found in petroleum products and most often contaminates drinking water by discharge from petroleum refineries.

Arsenic is a chemical element used in rat poison, agricultural insecticides, pesticides, and herbicides. Small amounts of arsenic are used in the production of electronics. Major sources in drinking water include naturally-occurring mineral deposits, orchard runoff, and industrial runoff from glass and electronics production.

compound_name_akas: AAtrex | Atranex | Atratol | Atred | Atrex | Attrex | Fenatrol | Griffex | Mebazine | Primatol A | Vectral SC | Weedex
sources: Atrazine is a synthetic herbicide widely used to control broadleaf weeds and grasses in agricultural crops. It enters the environment and drinking water supplies through agricultural application, runoff and leaching into groundwater and surface water.

Barium is a chemical element that is commonly used as a filler for rubber, plastics, and resins. Some of its compounds are used in signal flares, fireworks, drilling fluid, X-ray radiocontrast agents, and rodenticides. It is released from drilling and metal refining operations, and by erosion of natural mineral deposits.

Benzene is a gasoline range aromatic hydrocarbon (C6) found in petroleum and used as a solvent for fats, oils, inks, paints, rubber, and plastics, and as a chemical intermediate in the manufacture of detergents, explosives, pharmaceuticals, and dyestuffs. Benzene enters water sources via industrial discharge as well as leaching from fuel storage tanks and landfills.

Benzo[a]anthracene is a diesel-range PAH (C18) produced from incomplete combustion of organic materials and found in coal tar, roasted coffee, tobacco smoke, smoked foods, and automobile exhaust. There are no known uses of this compound other than research and it is not produced at scale.

compound_name_akas: B(a)P | 3,4-BP | 3,4-Benzopyrene | 3,4-Benzpyrene | BP | benzo[a]pyrene | benzo[def]chrysene | benzo[pqr]tetraphene | benzpyrene
sources: Benzo[a]pyrene is a diesel-range PAH (C20) commonly found in coal tar. It is also found in tobacco smoke, vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, and many foods such as grilled meats, as it is produced from incomplete combustion of organic materials. Benzo[a]pyrene is found in and leaches from asphalt that was historically used to line water storage tanks and distribution lines, which is its primary source as a drinking water contaminant.

Benzo[b]fluoranthene is a diesel-range PAH (C20) commonly found in fossil fuels and petroleum products. It is also found in tobacco smoke, vehicle exhaust, and industrial emissions as it is produced from incomplete combustion of organic materials.

Benzo[ghi]perylene is a diesel-range PAH (C22) commonly found in coal tar and crude oil. It is also found in tobacco smoke, vehicle exhaust, and industrial emissions as it is produced from incomplete combustion of organic materials.

Benzo[k]fluoranthene is a diesel-range PAH (C20) commonly found in coal tar and crude oil. It is also found in tobacco smoke, vehicle exhaust, and industrial emissions as it is produced from incomplete combustion of organic materials.

Benzo[k]tetraphene is a diesel-range PAH (C22) commonly found in coal tar and crude oil. It is also found in tobacco smoke, vehicle exhaust, and industrial emissions as it is produced from incomplete combustion of organic materials.

Beryllium is a chemical element naturally found in minerals, rocks, coal, soil, and volcanic dust. Its alloys with other metals are used as electrical components, tools, and structural components, especially in aircraft, missiles, and satellites. Beryllium can contaminate drinking water sources by release from industrial operations (coal-burning power plants and factories and the metal refining, electrical, aerospace, and defense industries).

compound_name_akas: BEHA | DEHA | Diethylhexyl adipate | Dioctyl adipate
sources: A synthetic organic compound widely used as a plasticizer to increase flexibility in plastics, particularly in polyvinyl chloride (PVC) food-packaging materials. As a solvent it is used as a component of aircraft lubricants and in hydraulic fluids. Bis(2-ethylhexyl)adipate contaminates drinking water through discharge from chemical factories.

Bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate is a synthetic organic compound widely used as a plasticizer to increase flexibility in plastics, particularly in polyvinyl chloride (PVC). It is also used as a hydraulic fluid and dielectric fluid in electrical capacitors. Bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate contaminates drinking water through discharge from chemical factories.

Bromate is an ion composed of bromine and oxygen. Bromate-containing compounds have a variety of uses, but it is present in drinking water most commonly as a disinfection byproduct produced by reaction of ozone, used as an anti-microbial treatment, with naturally occurring bromide.

Bromide is the anionic (negatively charged) form of bromine, a chemical element and halogen. It is most commonly found in seawater, some fossil fuels, and some relatively rarae minerals. In coastal regions, bromide levels in groundwater are usually higher than in inland areas, owing to seawater intrusion into the groundwater aquifer. Bromide in a water source can form bromine-containing disinfection byproducts when water is treated with an oxidizer such as free chlorine to kill microbes.

Bromobenzene is an organic compound commonly used as a solvent for large scale crystallization and as a reagent in organic synthesis. It is mainly found in chemical laboratories and industrial manufacturing processes, and is used in the production of pharmaceuticals and other organic chemicals.

compound_name_akas: CB | CBM | Chlorobromomethane | Fluorocarbon 1011 | Halon 1011 | Methyl chlorobromide | chloromethyl bromide | monochloromonobromomethane
sources: Bromochloromethane is a synthetic organic compound that is primarily used as a fire-extinguishing agent, as a solvent, and as an intermediate in the manufacture of some insecticides. It is mainly found in industrial fire protection systems and equipment.

sources: Bromodichloromethane is a synthetic organic compound and trihalomethane commonly formed as a disinfection byproduct when chlorine is used to treat water. It is also used as a reagent and intermediate in organic synthesis, as a fire extinguishing agent, a solvent for fats, waxes, and resins, and as a heavy liquid for mineral and salt separations.

npdwr_notes: MCL as a class, see TTHMs
sources: Bromoform is an organic compound and trihalomethane formed naturally by marine algae. It has been used as a solvent for waxes and oils, and in shipbuilding, aircraft, and aerospace industries and as a fire-suppressing chemical in fire extinguishers. In drinking water, bromoform is produced as a disinfection byproduct when certain disinfectants react with bromide naturally present in the source water.

Bromomethane is an organic compound produced naturally in small amounts by algae and kelp, and it is widely used as a soil fumigant and pesticide in agriculture. It is also used in industrial applications including chemical synthesis and as a refrigerant and fire extinguishing agent

compound_name_akas: 2-butanone | methyl ethyl ketone | MEK | butan-2-one | ethyl methyl ketone | methyl acetone | oxobutane
sources: 2-butanone is a common organic solvent used in processes involving gums, resins, cellulose materials, and surface coatings, and found in products like paints, varnishes, adhesives, and cleaning agents. It is also used in the synthetic rubber, plastics, and textiles industries, and for degreasing and oil extraction applications.

n-butylbenzene is a C10 aromatic hydrocarbon used in organic synthesis (including pesticide manufacturing), as a solvent for coating materials, and as a plasticizer, surface active agent, and polymer linking agent in plastic production. It is commonly found in asphalt and naphtha.

sec-butylbenzene is a C10 aromatic hydrocarbon used in organic synthesis, as a solvent for coating materials, and as a plasticizer and surface active agent. It can be found in crude oil, vehicle emissions, ambient air, and may be released heated plastics.
tert-butylbenzene is a C10 aromatic hydrocarbon used as a solvent and polymer-linking agent in organic synthesis. It has also been found in landfill gas.

Cadmium is a chemical element and metal used in electroplating, pigments, batteries, plastics, and corrosion-resistant coatings. It is also used in alloys, solders, Ni-Cd batteries, and nuclear reactor control systems, and can be released into the air through fossil fuel burning and waste incineration. Cadmium can be released into drinking water by corrosion of galvanized piping, erosion of natural minerals, and industrial discharge (metal refining, waste batteries & paints).

Calcium is a chemical element and metal. It is the fifth most abundant element in the earth’s crust and is a major component of many rocks and minerals, including the minerals that make up the shells of shellfish and the exoskeletons of corals. Calcium is an essential dietary mineral and is one of the water components that cause “hard” water. Evidence suggests that elevated calcium in drinking water may actually be beneficial to human health. Calcium in drinking water comes from the erosion of natural calcium-containing minerals.

sources: Carbon tetrachloride is a chemical compound that is an excellent solvent and was consequently used in a wide variety of applications; used broadly as a solvent, it is also non-flammable and was used as a fire extinguishing fluid, it also found use as a grain fumigant. Owing to its toxicity and environmental impact, especially its ozone-depleting nature, its use today has been greatly curtailed and continuing uses are highly regulated. It is used in the production of refrigerants and as a blowing agent. Carbon tetrachloride contaminantes drinking water through discharge from industrial activities.

Chlorate is an ion composed of chlorine and oxygen. It occurs naturally in some minerals and is used in a variety of  Chlorate-containing compounds have a variety of uses, but it is present in drinking water most commonly as a disinfection byproduct produced from the use of chlorine dioxide as an anti-microbial water treatment.

sources: alpha-chlordane is a synthetic compound and component of the pesticide chlordane. It was primarily used to control termites, agricultural pests, and household insects, but is now banned and restricted from use in the United States. Chlordane residue is highly persistent in the environment and is still found contaminating some drinking water sources today despite having been banned since 1988.
notes: Pure compound, not to be confused with chlordane as a product, which contains chlordane, heptachlor, and nonachlor

sources: gamma-chlordane is a synthetic organochlorine compound and component of the pesticide chlordane. It was primarily used to control termites, agricultural pests, and household insects, but it is now banned or limited to very restricted use and is no longer produced for commercial use in the United States. Chlordane residue is highly persistent in the environment and is still found contaminating some drinking water sources today despite having been banned since 1988.
notes: Pure compound, not to be confused with chlordane as a product, which contains chlordane, heptachlor, and nonachlor

sources: Chloride is the anionic (negatively charged) form of chlorine, a chemical element and halogen. It is a common ion found in rocks, soils, and is the major component of dietary salt (sodium chloride), which is the salt found in the ocean. Chloride is found in road salt and a large number of industrial and commercial chemicals. Chloride can be introduced into drinking water by dissolution of natural mineral deposits, infiltration of seawater into a well, and discharge from industrial processes or sewage. Chloride is naturally present in drinking water systems treated with free chlorine, which produces chloride as a product of certain reactions. Some other water treatment chemicals, including some water softener salts, also contain chloride. Elevated chloride in water may contribute to a salty taste.
Chlorine is added to drinking water to kill microbes that can cause disease. Excessive chlorine can be hazardous both directly and through increased disinfection byproduct formation.

Chlorite is an ion composed of chlorine and oxygen. It is used as a precursor to chlorine dioxide, which is used in water disinfection, and produced as a disinfection byproduct when chlorine dioxide is used to treat water. Note: While the term “chlorite” is also used to describe a group of minerals, these minerals do not contain any form of chlorine and are instead named for their green color (from the Greek chloros, meaning “green”).

compound_name_akas: MCB | PhCl | benzene chloride | phenyl chloride
sources: Chlorobenzene is a synthetic organic chemical compound used mainly as an industrial solvent and as an intermediate in the production of pesticides, herbicides, coatings such as bitumen and asphalt, and as an intermediate in the production of dyes, rubber, and pharmaceuticals. Chlorobenzene can contaminate drinking water sources through discharge from chemical factories.

Chloroethane is a synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon used as an industrial chemical intermediate and formerly used as a refrigerant and aerosol propellant. It is used as a solvent and in the manufacture of dyes, chemicals and foamed plastics.

Vinyl chloride is a synthetic organic chemical compound used primarily as a chemical intermediate in the production of polyvinyl chloride (PVC), a material used in automotive parts, packaging, plumbing, furniture, and construction materials. Contamination of drinking water by vinyl chloride occurs by leaching from PVC pipes and discharge from plastic factories. Vinyl chloride has recently been in the public eye as a result of the 2023 East Palestine, OH train derailment.

npdwr_notes: MCL as a class, see TTHMs
sources: Chloroform is a synthetic organic compound used as an industrial solvent and as an intermediate in the production of refrigerants and fluoropolymers. It is mainly used in controlled industrial processes including chemical manufacturing and laboratory applications. Chloroform is also formed as a disinfection byproduct when chlorine in the drinking water system reacts with dissolved organic matter.

Chloromethane is a volatile organic compound primarily used as a chemical intermediate in the production of silicones and methylcellulose. It is also used in extraction of greases, oils, and resins, and as a herbicide

2-chlorotoluene is a chlorinated hydrocarbon used as a chemical intermediate and as a solvent in the manufacturing of agrochemicals such as dye production, pesticides, and household draining products.

4-chlorotoluene is a chlorinated hydrocarbon used as an intermediate in the manufacturing of dyes, pesticides and pharmaceutical compounds. It is also used as a solvent in coatings such as paints, varnishes, lacquers, and sealants.

Chromium is a chemical element and metal. It is primarily used in stainless steel and “chrome plating” of other metals. Chromium is also used in leather tanning, ceramics & glasses, photography, fungicides, and certain catalysts. Chromium in drinking water occurs as one of two ions, Cr(III) with 3+ charge and Cr(VI) with a 6+ charge. Cr(III) is a non-toxic dietary mineral found naturally in many foods. Cr(VI) is hazardous to human health, occurring naturally in certain minerals and artificially as a result of industrial activity.

Chrysene is a diesel range polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) found in coal tar and formed as a byproduct of incomplete combustion of organic materials. It is primarily used as a research chemical and as a component of creosote.

Conductivity is a measurement of the ability of a water sample to pass electrical current, which is related to the amount of charged particles (ions) present in the water. Because conductivity can be measured very inexpensively, it is a good screening measurement that can indicate the presence of elevated salts, acids, or other charged contaminants. A conductivity measurement can not detect a specific contaminant but can indicate the need for further testing and water treatment.

Copper is a chemical element and metal that is widely used in electrical wiring and plumbing. It is also used in alloys, coatings and can be released into the environment through mining, smelting and industrial processes. Copper in drinking water is most often present due to corrosion of copper piping or erosion of natural minerals.

1,2-dibromo-3-chloropropane is an organic compound that was widely used as a soil fumigant in agriculture to control nematodes. Its usage has been discontinued due to health risk, except as an intermediate in chemical synthesis. DBCP can still be found in drinking water as a result of persistent residue from historical agricultural operations. On Oʻahu, DBCP was used as a nematocide in pineapple plantations from the 1940s to 1980s. It is commonly found in groundwater in former agricultural areas and is removed by filtration with granular activated carbon (GAC).
See total haloacetic acids

sources: Dibromochloromethane is an organic compound formed as a disinfection byproduct when chlorine reacts with natural organic matter in source water. It is also used as a laboratory reagent, and formerly was used as a flame retardant and chemical intermediate.

1,2-dibromoethane is a synthetic hydrocarbon that was widely used as a soil fumigant and as an additive to leaded gasoline. It is currently used as a pesticide and as an intermediate for dyes, resins, waxes and gums. The principal source of drinking water contamination is discharge from petroleum refineries.
Dibromomethane is an organic compound used as a solvent, in fire extinguishing fluids, and in chemical synthesis. It occurs naturally in ocean environments where it is produced by marine algae.
See total haloacetic acids

o-dichlorobenzene is a chlorinated hydrocarbon used as a chemical intermediate, solvent in industrial processes, and in the production of insecticides and deodorizing products. It is used in lubricants, greases, paints, and coatings. o-dichlorobenzene contaminates drinking water through discharge from chemical factories.
m-dichlorobenzene is a chlorinated hydrocarbon used mainly as a chemical intermediate in the manufacturing of herbicides, insecticides, dyes and other industrial chemicals.

p-dichlorobenzene is a chlorinated hydrocarbon commonly used in mothballs and deodorizer blocks. It is also used as a chemical intermediate in the production of pesticides, dyes and other industrial products. p-dichlorobenzene contaminates drinking water through discharge from chemical factories.

sources: Dichlorodifluoromethane is a synthetic chlorofluorocarbon compound used mainly as a refrigerant in air conditioners and refrigerators, an aerosol propellant, and a blowing agent in foam manufacturing.

compound_name_akas: 1,1-Ethylidene dichloride | Asymmetrical dichloroethane | CFC-150a | ethylidene dichloride
sources: 1,1-dichloroethane is a synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon used mainly as a solvent and a chemical intermediate in the production of plastics, oils, cleaning agents, and other industrial chemicals. It is also used as an insecticide spray, and as a solvent for paints and varnishes.

compound_name_akas: 1,2-DCE | DCA | DCE | EDC | alpha,beta-dichloroethane | ethane dichloride | ethylene dichloride
sources: 1,2-dichloroethane is a synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon mainly used in the production of vinyl chloride and other chemicals. It is also used as a solvent in degreasing applications, cleaning products, and industrial chemical processes. 1,2-dichloroethane contaminates drinking water through discharge from chemical factories.
1,1-dichloroethylene is a synthetic organic chemical used in the production of polymers and high purity silica films.

cis-1,2-dichloroethene is a synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon  commonly formed through breakdown of other halogenated hydrocarbons in waste water and anaerobic groundwater. It is mainly used as a solvent in the extraction of oils, resins and lacquers, and it is also a chemical intermediate. cis-1,2-dichloroethene contaminates drinking water through discharge from chemical factories.
Mixture of cis- and trans-1,2-dichloroethene - see individual compounds for source information.

trans-1,2-dichloroethene is a synthetic chlorinated hydrocarbon used as a solvent for extracting oils, fats, and resins and in cleaning and degreasing industrial materials. trans-1,2-dichloroethene contaminates drinking water through discharge from chemical factories.

1,2-dichloropropane is an organic compound produced as a byproduct of the production of epichlorohydrin. It is used as a chemical intermediate in the production of other organic chemicals, as an industrial solvent, and in petroleum processing.
1,3-dichloropropane is a synthetic volatile organic compound that is found as a contaminant in soil fumigants containing 1,3-dichloropropene. It has no known uses or intentional production.

2,2-dichloropropane is a chlorinated organic compound used as a solvent for pesticides in agriculture and as an industrial solvent. It is also used in organic synthesis and in isomerization catalyst processes saturated hydrocarbons.

1,1-dichloropropene is a synthetic volatile organic compound. Minimal information is available on its uses. The USEPA investigated regulation of this compound in the early 2000s after environmental data collected nationwide in the late 1990s found that it was present in at least some drinking water sources. However, no regulation was ever promulgated and the compound was dropped from further consideration after 2008.

compound_name_akas: AQL Agrocelhone, DD92, 1,3-D, Dorlone, Nematox, Telone, Nemex, Di-Trapex CP, Vorlex 201, chloroallylchloride, DCP
sources: 1,3-dichloropropene is a synthetic volatile organic compound mainly used as a soil fumigant pesticide to control nematodes and other soil pests in agricultural settings. It is commonly applied before planting crops and may be released into the environment through agricultural use, spills and industrial handling. 1,3-dichloropropene consists of two isomers, cis-1,3-dichloropropene and trans-1,3-dichloropropene.

cis-1,3-dichloropropene is a chlorinated organic compound and one isomer of 1,3-dichloropene. It is used mainly as a soil fumigant pesticide to control nematodes and other soil pests in agricultural settings.
trans-1,3-dichloropropene is a chlorinated organic compound and one isomer of 1,3-dichloropropene. It is used mainly as a soil fumigant pesticide in agricultural settings.

Diisopropyl ether is an organic ether compound used mainly as an industrial solvent and as an additive in gasoline to improve engine performance. It is also used in extraction processes and organic synthesis.

Endrin is an organochlorine compound formerly used as a pesticide to control insects, rodents, and birds on agricultural crops such as cotton and grains. Its use has been banned or severely restricted in many countries due to its toxicity, but residue may persist in the environment and contaminate drinking water sources.
Ethyl tert-butyl ether is an organic compound used mainly as a gasoline additive to improve fuel combustion efficiency. It is also used as an oxygenate to increase gasoline octane levels.

Ethylbenzene is a C8 (gasoline range) hydrocarbon found in a variety of petroleum products and used in the production of styrene. It is also used as an anti-knock agent in gasolines to increase octane rating and prevent engine knocking.

Fluoranthene is a diesel range (C16) polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) found in fossil fuels and formed during incomplete combustion of organic materials. It is commonly found in coal, tar, creosote, asphalt, vehicle exhaust, cigarette smoke and has been used as a chemical intermediate in the production of dyes and pesticides.

Fluorene is a diesel range (C13) polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) formed primarily during incomplete combustion and found in coal tar, crude oil and petroleum products. It is used in the production of dyes, pharmaceuticals, plastics and other specialty chemicals. Small amounts of fluorene have been reported in JP-5 jet fuel.
notes: Not to be confused with fluorine, chemical element, symbol F

sources: Fluoride is the anionic (negatively charged) form of fluorine, a chemical element and halogen. It is a common ion found in rocks and soils, and is commonly found in small amounts in drinking water sources due to erosion of natural deposits. Small amounts of fluoride are also added to drinking water by some utilities to promote dental health.
notes: Anion form of the chemical element fluorine, not to be confused with the PAH fluorene

compound_name_akas: 1,1,2-trichloro-1,2,2-trifluoroethane | CFC-113 | TTE | chlorofluorocarbon-113 | freon 113 | halocarbon 113 | refrigerant 113 | trichlorotrifluoroethane
sources: Freon 113 is a synthetic chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) formerly used as an industrial solvent for cleaning and degreasing electronic components, metals, and precision equipment. It was also used in refrigeration and aerosol applications. Its use has been phased out due to its ozone-depleting effects.

Heptachlor is a synthetic organochlorine compound that was widely used to control soil insects, termites, ants, and agricultural pests on crops. Its use has been banned or severely restricted in many countries but residue may still be found in soil, sediments, and the environment, including drinking water sources, due to past applications.

Heptachlor epoxide is a chlorinated organic compound formed when the pesticide heptachlor breaks down in the environment or within living organisms. It has no major commercial use of its own but is commonly found in soil, sediments, water and wildlife due to historical use of heptachlor and is highly persistent in the environment.

Heterotrophs are organisms that can not produce their own food and instead rely on consuming other food sources to survive. A heterotrophic plate count measurement is performed by placing a water sample on a petri dish (plate) containing a food source, incubating the plate for some time, and counting how many bacterial colonies form. This provides information about the number of live bacteria in the water, which can indicate whether pathogenic bacteria could be present.

stockholm_convention_status: A (as industrial chemical), C (as unintentional production)
sources: Hexachlorobutadiene is a chlorinated organic compound commonly produced as a byproduct during the manufacture of chlorinated hydrocarbons. It has been used as an industrial solvent and is currently used in manufacture of rubber compounds and other chlorinated chemicals.

compound_name_akas: gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane | gamma-HCH | gammaxene | Gammallin | benzene hexachloride
sources: Lindane is a synthetic organochlorine insecticide that was used to control agricultural pests on crops and livestock and treat head lice and scabies in humans. Its agricultural use has been banned or restricted due to environmental and health concerns, but residue may persist in the environment and contaminate drinking water sources.

Hexachlorocyclopentadiene is an organochlorine compound used primarily as a chemical intermediate in the manufacture of organochlorine pesticides, including aldrin, dieldrin, endrin, chlordane and heptachlor. Hexachlorocyclopentadiene contaminates drinking water through discharge from chemical factories and as residue in pesticide formulations.

2-hexanone is an organic compound primarily used as an industrial solvent in coatings, paints, adhesives, and chemical manufacturing processes. 2-hexanone can be released into the environment through industrial emissions, solvent use, spills, and waste disposal.

Indeno[1,2,3-cd]pyrene is a diesel range (C22) polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) formed during incomplete combustion of organic materials. It is commonly found in vehicle exhaust, coal tar, soot, cigarette smoke and polluted air, water and soil.

Iron is a chemical element and metal. It is the fourth most abundant element in the earth’s crust and is a major component of many rocks and minerals, especially basalts like those that form the Hawaiian Islands. Iron is an important dietary mineral found in foods, especially red meats. Iron in drinking water can come from the erosion of iron-containing minerals, but also from the erosion of piping materials containing iron (especially cast iron). Excess iron can cause a metallic taste, a rusty color, red/orange staining of water-contact surfaces, and formation of sediments in plumbing.

p-isopropyltoluene is a C10 aromatic hydrocarbon found naturally in plants including cranberries, cumin and thyme. It is manufactured from petrochemical feedsticks through the alkylation of toluene with propylene. It is used as a solvent and chemical intermediate in the production of fragrances, metal polishes, thinners for lacquers/varnishes, synthetic resins, and other industrial chemicals.

Lead is a chemical element and heavy metal primarily used in lead-acid batteries for vehicles and backup power systems. It is also used in ammunition, radiation shielding for medical and industrial applications, construction materials, cable coverings, solder and various metal products. The principal sources of lead contamination in drinking water are corrosion of lead piping and erosion of natural minerals.

Magnesium is a chemical element and metal. It is the seventh most abundant element in the earth’s crust and is a major component of many rocks and minerals. Magnesium is an essential dietary mineral and is one of the water components that cause “hard” water. Evidence suggests that elevated magnesium in drinking water may actually be beneficial to human health. Magnesium in drinking water comes from the erosion of natural magnesium-containing minerals.

Manganese is a chemical element and metal. It is a common component of minerals and is present in some drinking water treatment chemicals. Manganese is an essential dietary mineral and is also used in a number of industrial processes and products, including steels, fertilizers, batteries, cosmetics, and fireworks. Excessive manganese in drinking water can cause a black or brown color, black staining of water-contact surfaces, and a bitter metallic taste.

Mercury is a chemical element and metal used in scientific and industrial instruments, electrical switches and relays, fluorescent and mercury-vapor lamps, and some manufacturing processes. It has also been used in thermometers, barometers, dental amalgams, and gold mining. The principal sources of mercury contamination in drinking water are discharges from industrial operations (refineries, factories, landfills, and croplands) and erosion of natural deposits.

Methoxychlor is a synthetic organochlorine insecticide that was used to control flies, mosquitoes, roaches, and agricultural pests on crops, livestock, and domestic animals. It was commonly used in public health pest control, animal management, and agricultural programs prior to being banned in 2003. Residue may persist and contaminate drinking water sources.

Methyl tert-butyl ether/MTBE is a synthetic organic compound used primarily as a gasoline additive to increase octane rating and improve combustion efficiency. It is also used as a solvent in both industrial and research applications.

4-methyl-2-pentanone is an organic compound primarily used as an industrial solvent in paints, coatings, varnishes, lacquers, adhesives, inks, and resins. It is also used in the production of pharmaceuticals, rubber products, and chemical intermediates, and in extraction and cleaning processes.

Methylene chloride is a synthetic chlorinated organic compound primarily used as an industrial solvent in paint strippers, metal cleaning and degreasing, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and chemical processing. It is also used in aerosol formulations, foam productions, and the manufacture of plastics and other industrial products. Dichloromethane contaminates drinking water through discharge from chemical factories.

1-methylnaphthalene is a diesel range (C11) polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) commonly found in fossil fuels, including JP-5 jet fuel. It is used in chemical research, as an intermediate in the manufacture of dyes and specialty chemicals, and as a component of fuels and lubricants.

2-methylnaphthalene is a diesel range (C11) polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) commonly found in fossil fuels, including JP-5 jet fuel. It is used as a chemical intermediate in the production of dyes, resins and other chemicals and is also a component of fuels, lubricants and industrial petroleum products.

Naphthalene is a diesel range (C10) polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) primarily used in the production of other chemicals, chiefly phthalic anhydride, but also pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and other compounds. Naphthalene is also used in mothballs and deodorizer blocks, and is known to be present in JP-5 jet fuel.

Nickel is a chemical element and metal primarily used in the production of stainless steel and other metal alloys. It is also used in batteries, electroplating, coins, electronics, catalysts and industrial machinery.

sources: cis-nonachlor is a chlorinated organic compound that is found in the pesticide chlordane, which was applied to control termites, soil insects, and agricultural pests. Chlordane use has been banned since 1988, but residue may persist in the environment.

sources: trans-nonachlor is a chlorinated organic compound and a major component of the pesticide chlordane, which was widely used to control termites, soil insects, and agricultural pests. Chlordane use has been banned since 1988, but residue may persist in the environment.

Pentachlorophenol is a synthetic chlorinated organic compound primarily used as a wood preservative to protect utility poles, railroad ties, fence posts, and other outdoor products from fungal decay and insect damage. It has also been used as a pesticide, herbicide, and fungicide. Recently, the USEPA proposed a total ban on pentachlorophenol use in the USA; as of this writing, the phase-out period is ongoing. Drinking water contamination by pentachlorophenol can occur as a result of release from treated wood products or the factories which prepare them.

pH is a measure of the concentration of hydrogen ions in water, which indicates the acidity (low pH) or basicity (high pH) of the water. Excessively low pH can cause a bitter or metallic taste in drinking water and corrode plumbing fixtures; excessively high pH can cause water to have a slippery feel, a soda taste, and excessive deposits around plumbing.

Phenanthrene is a diesel range (C14) polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) found naturally in fossil fuels and formed during incomplete combustion of organic materials. It is used as an intermediate in the production of dyes, plastics, pesticides, pharmaceuticals and other specialty chemicals. Small amounts of phenanthrene have been reported in JP-5 jet fuel.

Phosphate is an ion composed of phosphorus and oxygen and a component of many minerals, including the mineral hydroxyapatite, which makes up bones and teeth.. Low levels of phosphate are common in drinking water from erosion of natural deposits, and additional phosphate may be added as a corrosion control measure to prevent leaching of lead from lead-containing plumbing materials. Phosphate is also used in fertilizers and elevated phosphate in drinking water may be due to agricultural runoff.

Potassium is a chemical element and metal. It is the eighth most abundant element in the earth’s crust and is a major component of many rocks and minerals. Potassium is found naturally in many foods and is an essential nutrient. Potassium is present in drinking water from erosion of natural potassium-containing minerals and the use of some potassium-containing chemicals in water treatment, but there is no evidence that potassium levels in municipal, treated drinking water are ever high enough to cause a health hazard to consumers.

Isopropylbenzene is an aromatic organic compound primarily used as a chemical intermediate to produce phenol and acetone. It is also used as a solvent and is a component of petroleum fuels, including JP-5 jet fuel.

n-propylbenzene is a gasoline range (C9) aromatic hydrocarbon used as a solvent and as an intermediate in the manufacture of other chemicals, including plastics, resins, and specialty industrial products. It is also found in petroleum products, including JP-5 jet fuel.

Pyrene is a diesel range (C16) polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) found in coal tar and formed during incomplete combustion of coal, oil, gasoline, wood and other organic materials. It is primarily used in chemical research and as an intermediate in the production of dyes, plastics, pesticides and other specialty chemicals and commonly found in coal tar, petroleum products and combustion emissions.

Selenium is a chemical element used in electronics, glass manufacturing, pigments, solar cells, and metal alloys. It is also used in semiconductor production, photocopiers, batteries, and as an additive in some industrial and agricultural products. Drinking water contamination arises from industrial discharges (petroleum and metal refineries, mining) and erosion of natural minerals.

Silica is a chemical compound that is a major component of many minerals, rocks, and sands, especially quartz, which makes up more than 10% of the earth’s crust. Silica is also naturally present in some plants such as rice. The primary uses of silica are in production of concrete, glass, and pure silicon. Silica is also used in drinking water treatment to make sand filters and prepare sodium silicate, which is used to help coagulate impurities so that they settle out of the water. Water that is high in silica can contribute to formation of scale or sediment and exhibit persistent cloudiness.

Simazine is an herbicide used to control broadleaf weeds and grasses in agriculture, orchards, vineyards, and non-crop areas. It is commonly applied to crops and landscaped areas to prevent weed growth and it enters the environment through agricultural use, runoff and leaching into soil and water.

Sodium is a chemical element and metal. It is the sixth most abundant element in the earth’s crust and is a major component of many rocks and minerals, most notably dietary salt (sodium chloride), which is also the salt found in the oceans. Sodium is found naturally in many foods and is an essential nutrient, though excessive consumption of sodium can lead to health problems and is especially common in the developed world. Sodium is present in drinking water owing to its almost ubiquitous presence in water sources as well as its use as a component of various water treatment chemicals. Excessively high sodium levels can arise from contamination by seawater, road salt, fertilizers, industrial waste, or sewage.

Styrene is an aromatic organic compound primarily used in the production of polystyrene plastics (including styrofoam and ABS), synthetic rubber (including ~50% of tire rubber production), fiberglass, resins, and insulation materials. Sources of drinking water contamination include discharges from factories that employ styrene in the production of rubber and plastics and leaching from landfills.

Sulfate is an ion composed of sulfur and oxygen and a component of many minerals. It is most commonly found in water through erosion of natural deposits. Excessive amounts of sulfate may cause a salty or bitter taste.

tert-amyl methyl ether/TAME is an organic compound primarily used as a gasoline additive to increase octane levels and improve fuel combustion efficiency. It is added to gasoline to reduce engine knocking and help lower emissions from motor vehicles.

1,1,1,2-tetrachloroethane is a chlorinated organic compound primarily used as a solvent in the production of wood stains and varnishes and in insecticides and paint removers. It has been used in metal degreasing, extraction processes, and chemical manufacturing, and serves as a feedstock for the production of solvents and refrigerants.

1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane is a chlorinated organic compound primarily used as an industrial solvent for fats, oils, waxes, resins, and rubber. It has also been used as a chemical intermediate in the manufacture of other chlorinated compounds and in metal cleaning, degreasing and extraction processes.

It is also used as solvent in textile processing, chemical manufacturing and the production of other industrial chemicals. Drinking water contamination can occur as a result of discharge from factories and dry cleaners.

Thallium is a chemical element that occurs naturally in the earth’s crust and is used in a variety of electronics and optics applications, especially in scientific research. It occurs in ores that are sources of lead, zinc, and copper, and is produced as a byproduct of their refining. Thallium contamination of drinking water can occur through leaching from ore-processing sites and discharge from factories that handle thallium compounds (electronics, glass, and drugs).

Toluene is a gasoline range (C7) aromatic hydrocarbon primarily used as a gasoline additive and as an industrial solvent in paints, coatings, adhesives, inks and cleaning products. It is also used as a precursor to the production of benzene and xylenes. Toluene is known to be present in JP-5 jet fuel.

Total alkalinity is a measurement of all substances that can neutralize acids in a water sample, most commonly carbonate, bicarbonate, and hydroxide ions. High concentrations of these ions arise naturally from leaching of certain minerals from rocks and soils, and through certain industrial processes. Alkalinity is related to, but not the same as, water hardness.

Coliforms are a family of bacteria common in the digestive tracts and feces of warm-blooded animals. While many coliforms are not themselves hazardous (a notable exception to this being certain strains of E. coli), they are easily measured, so their presence in water is used as a surrogate for the presence of harder-to-measure disease-causing bacteria. Fecal coliforms are a subset of total coliforms that are found exclusively in feces.

Haloacetic acids (HAAs) are disinfection byproducts formed through reaction of disinfectants with organic material present in source water. Five haloacetic acids are regulated under federal guidelines: monochloroacetic acid, dichloroacetic acid, trichloroacetic acid, monobromo acetic acid, and dibromoacetic acid.

Total organic carbon is a measure of the quantity of the chemical element carbon present in a sample that is present in organic compounds. Organic compounds are those compounds that contain carbon-carbon and carbon-hydrogen bonds. Carbon comes from a huge number of sources and measured total organic carbon can not be definitively linked to any particular source without additional chemical analysis. Organic carbon is commonly present in drinking water sources at low levels from dissolved natural materials and bacterial metabolites. Total organic carbon is monitored and controlled to manage production of disinfection byproducts in the drinking water system.

Trihalomethanes (THMs) are compounds consisting of a central carbon atom which is bound to one hydrogen atom and three atoms of chlorine, bromine, or iodine. They are produced in drinking water as result of water treatment with chlorine and the presence of naturally-occurring bromide and/or iodide. Four trihalomethanes (trichloromethane, bromodichloromethane, dibromochloromethane, and tribromomethane) are regulated drinking water contaminants as a mixture, measured as total trihalomethanes/TTHMs, also sometimes notated as trihalomethanes-4/THM4s.

1,2,3-trichlorobenzene is an organochlorine compound primarily used as a chemical intermediate in the manufacture of dyes, pesticides, insecticides, lubricants and other industrial chemicals. It has also been used as a solvent, dielectric fluid and heat-transfer medium in industrial applications.

1,2,4-trichlorobenzene is an organochlorine compound primarily used as a chemical intermediate in the production of dyes, herbicides, insecticides, and other industrial chemicals. It has also been used as a solvent, degreasing agent, dielectric fluid, heat-transfer medium and lubricant additive. Contamination of drinking water with 1,2,4-trichlorobenzene most frequently occurs as a result of discharges from textile finishing factories.

sources: 1,1,1-trichloroethane is an organochlorine compound that was widely used as an industrial solvent for metal degreasing, cleaning electronic components and removing oils, greases and adhesives. It was also used in aerosol products, coatings, inks, and chemical manufacturing processes before its use was largely phased out due to its ozone-depleting characteristics. Contamination of drinking water with 1,1,1-trichloroethane occurs as a result of discharge from industrial sites.

1,1,2-trichloroethane is an organochlorine compound primarily used as an industrial solvent and as a chemical intermediate in the manufacture of chlorinated chemicals. It has also been used as a solvent and in industrial processing applications. Contamination of drinking water with 1,1,1-trichloroethane occurs as a result of discharge from industrial sites.

Trichloroethene is an organochlorine compound primarily used as an industrial solvent for metal degreasing and cleaning of manufactured parts. It is also used in the production of refrigerants and in adhesives, paint removers, and industrial cleaning products.

Trichlorofluoromethane is a synthetic chlorofluorocarbon (CFC) primarily used as a refrigerant in air conditioning and refrigeration systems, as a blowing agent in the manufacture of foam insulation and packaging materials, and as a propellant in aerosol products.

1,2,3-trichloropropane is a chlorinated hydrocarbon compound used as a chemical intermediate in the production of pesticides and other industrial chemicals. It has also been used as a paint and varnish remover, degreasing agent, and cleaning solvent.

1,2,4-trimethylbenzene is an organic compound and gasoline range hydrocarbon (C9) found in coal tar and petroleum products, including JP-5 jet fuel. It is used in the production of polymers, dyes, perfumes, resins, and fuels. It is also used as a sterilizing agent and in laboratory experiments to measure radiation.

1,3,5-trimethylbenzene is an organic compound and gasoline range hydrocarbon (C9) found in coal tar and petroleum products. It is known to be present in JP-5 jet fuel and is used as a solvent, cleanser, and as a starting material for the production of other compounds.

Turbidity is a measurement of the cloudiness of a water sample. High turbidity indicates the presence of large particles, possibly including disease-causing organisms. Increased turbidity in drinking water is often due to the presence of soil runoff. A turbidity measurement can not detect a specific contaminant but can indicate the need for further testing and water treatment.

m- and p-xylene are C8 (gasoline range) hydrocarbons found in a variety of petroleum products including aviation fuels (including JP-5) and gasoline. m- and p-xylene are often found in a mixture with o-xylene (see xylenes, total). The vast majority of pure p-xylene produced is used to create PET plastic, which is used to make drink bottles, and polyester fabrics. m-xylene is used as a chemical precursor at a much smaller scale. Contamination of water sources by xylenes occurs by discharge from petroleum and chemical factories.
notes: m- and p-xylene are two structurally similar, but distinct chemical compounds. They are reported together because they are so similar that the standard method used for volatile organic compounds analysis, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, is unable to distinguish between them. The measured amount of "m- and p-xylene" in a sample may consist entirely of one compound or of a mixture of both.

sources: o-xylene is a C8 (gasoline range) hydrocarbon found in a variety of petroleum products including aviation fuels (including JP-5) and gasoline.  o-xylene is often found mixed with m- and p-xylenes (see xylenes, total); on its own, o-xylene is used to produce an intermediate used to make plasticizers. Contamination of water sources by xylenes occurs by discharge from petroleum and chemical factories.

Xylenes are a group of three related compounds, o-xylene, m-xylene, and p-xylene, which are C8 (gasoline range) hydrocarbons found in a variety of petroleum products including aviation fuels (including JP-5) and gasoline. The mixture of the three xylenes is used as an industrial solvent, as a thinner for paints and varnishes, and in dentistry. The vast majority of pure p-xylene produced is used to create PET plastic, which is used to make drink bottles, and polyester fabrics; o-xylene is used to produce an intermediate used to make plasticizers. Contamination of water sources by xylenes occurs by discharge from petroleum and chemical factories.
